clue.text: Five characters evidently following revolutionary piano course

indicators.note: the five-character run is placed after the revolutionary and the piano letter

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly
S, T, U, V, W are five letters of the alphabet, i.e. the run from S to W

explanation.surface: Someone describes a five-letter abbreviation coming after a revolutionary course for pianists.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading the five letters S T U V W as 'S to W'. 'Course' is a racecourse: Chepstow is a Welsh racecourse in Monmouthshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Chepstow is a horse-racing venue, and crosswords often use course for a racecourse.

clue.text: Firm that originally rejected protective cover

parts.note: firm means hard, solid

indicators.note: the original, i.e. first, letter of the word that is thrown out

explanation.surface: A company that turned down an initial proposal for protective insurance cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but is the adjective. 'Originally rejected' drops the first T of THAT, leaving HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard hat is the rigid helmet worn on building sites to protect the head.

clue.text: Separatists spout about forbidding pop music essentially

indicators.note: about signals that the word for spout is turned round

parts.note: the lip of a jug is its spout, where it pours
forbidding means grim, stern-looking
pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: the essence of the word music is its central letter

explanation.surface: Dissenters rant against banning popular music at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout about' reads as ranting on a subject, but 'about' turns the jug's spout round; 'essentially' takes just the heart of 'music'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pilgrim Fathers who sailed on the Mayflower were Separatists, Puritans who broke away from the Church of England.

clue.text: His mentor scattered particles in vacuum tubes?

indicators.note: letters scattered are strewn about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A student's tutor dispersed particles, like a physicist experimenting with valves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattered' rearranges HISMENTOR. The question mark marks the definition as an example: thermions are emitted in valves, among other places.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermions are charged particles given off by a hot body, the electrons that flow in thermionic valves.

clue.text: Beginning to rake in loads of money in minor charges

indicators.note: in tells us the first letter goes inside the money word

parts.note: wads are thick bundles of banknotes

indicators.note: the beginning of the word rake is its first letter

explanation.surface: Raking in big money from small fees for minor offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor charges' suggests petty criminal counts or small fees, but it means children in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Wards are minors placed under the protection of a guardian or court, i.e. their charges.

clue.text: "The lady ain't for turning" — the initial form of Thatcher's mantra

definitions.text: the initial form of Thatcher's mantra

indicators.note: turning the letters of the word round gives a new order, echoing Thatcher's line

explanation.surface: A play on Thatcher's 'The lady's not for turning', setting it beside her other famous slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For turning' rearranges AINT. 'The lady' hints at a woman's name, Tina, and perhaps Tina Turner; Thatcher's slogan was 'There Is No Alternative'.
explanation.definitionFit: TINA is the acronym of 'There is no alternative', Margaret Thatcher's favourite political slogan.

clue.text: During economic upswing nurses primarily lost out

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold closely, so the boom holds a letter inside

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic growth

indicators.note: primarily signals the word lost gives only its first letter

explanation.surface: In a time of prosperity, nursing staff mostly missed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like part of 'lost out' but is the definition: flowers that are out are blooming. 'Nurses' puts L, the start of 'lost', inside BOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is out has opened its flowers, which is to be in bloom.

clue.text: After metamorphosis, Samsa leaves

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Gregor Samsa, from Kafka's Metamorphosis, departs after his transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about Samsa departing; it is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a strong black tea from north-east India, sold as dried tea leaves.

clue.text: Despondent men didn't show up at work

indicators.note: letters at work are busy rearranging themselves into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that the workforce didn't turn up to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At work' reads as the place they failed to attend, but it shuffles MENDIDNTSHOWUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To be down in the dumps is an idiom for being gloomy and dejected.

clue.text: One conditionally released gets a job in gym

indicators.note: in places the job pieces inside the gym letters

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
a role is a job or function

explanation.surface: A prisoner let out on licence finds work at a gym.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is a prisoner freed early on parole, subject to conditions of good behaviour.

clue.text: Satisfied with fruit drop

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
met as in 'met the requirements', satisfied them

explanation.surface: Someone content with the fruit that has fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply and suddenly, a sharp drop.

clue.text: Native Australians overcoming fetish about bush tea

indicators.note: overcoming is read as coming over, enclosing the turned charm word

parts.note: roos, short for kangaroos, are animals native to Australia

indicators.note: about turns the charm word round

parts.note: obi, or obeah, is a West Indian fetish or charm

explanation.surface: Aboriginal Australians overcoming an obsession with drinking a herbal tea from the bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native Australians' suggests people but means the animals; 'about' turns the charm word round before 'overcoming' wraps them round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooibos, or redbush, is a South African shrub whose leaves make a caffeine-free herbal tea.

clue.text: Escort drug dealer out of Portugal

indicators.note: the Portugal letter is taken out of the dealer word

parts.note: a pusher sells illegal drugs
P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A drug dealer being escorted out of Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher shows people to their seats, escorting or guiding them.

clue.text: 50% of girls in class give incorrect responses

indicators.note: fifty per cent keeps only the first half of the girls word

parts.note: misses are young girls
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: Half the girls in a class answer wrongly.
explanation.definitionFit: To misinform is to give someone false information, here wrong answers.

clue.text: Old hit number I am performing with matron

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on an act in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A singer explains that they are doing a number with a matron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' reads as a song but is fodder. Mr Tambourine Man, written by Bob Dylan, was a 1965 number one for the Byrds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Tambourine Man was a chart-topping 1960s single, so a song from long ago.

clue.text: Historical African island, one to the north of Angola

indicators.note: in a down entry, being north of means coming above, so earlier

parts.note: Rhodes is a Greek island
I is the Roman numeral one
AN is taken as an abbreviation for Angola, though AO is the standard code

explanation.surface: Describing an African island lying to the north of Angola.
explanation.walkthrough: AN for Angola is a loose abbreviation; the official code is AO.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rhodesian belonged to Rhodesia, the country renamed Zimbabwe in 1980, so now only historical.

clue.text: Oral massage perfect, but not entirely necessary

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so we want a word sounding like the massage word

parts.note: to knead is to massage with the hands

indicators.note: not entirely means the perfect word loses its last letter

parts.note: full can mean complete or perfect, as in full marks

explanation.surface: A spoken massage was perfect, though not entirely required.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' looks like part of the definition but it trims FULL to FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful is an old-fashioned word meaning required or essential.

clue.text: Ominous heathens demolished residence of London dignitary

indicators.note: a demolished building is knocked apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Sinister heathens knocked down the home of a London official.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mansion House is the official home of the Lord Mayor of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Mayor of London lives at the Mansion House, the official residence of that office.

clue.text: Composer ignored by a novelist and painter

indicators.note: the composer is ignored by the letter a, which leaves him

parts.note: Edward Elgar, the English composer
Umberto Eco, the Italian novelist

explanation.surface: A composer snubbed by a novelist and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignored by a' is an odd construction: the A leaves ELGAR, giving ELGR.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Greek-born Renaissance artist who worked in Toledo, Spain.

clue.text: In difficult situation having finished active service?

parts.note: up means over or finished, as in 'time is up'
the service tree is a tree related to the rowan

explanation.surface: A soldier in a tight spot after completing active military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Active service' reads as military duty; split it. The question mark flags 'service' as an example of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Up a tree is an idiom for being stuck in a predicament, like a cat that cannot climb down.

clue.text: Somebody's providing ample food

parts.note: ample means big, large
cheese is a food

explanation.surface: A person is supplying generous amounts of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somebody' is the noun: a person of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cheese is slang for an important person, someone who is a somebody.

clue.text: Northerner who sings bass given choice of court cards

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music
a choice of jack or king, the court cards J and K: J OR K

explanation.surface: A northern bass singer is dealt picture cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sings bass' reads as one phrase; split it. The court cards are written J OR K.
explanation.definitionFit: Björk is the Icelandic singer, so a singer from the far north.

clue.text: Sea rangers regularly observed seabirds

indicators.note: only letters at regular intervals are looked at, every second one

explanation.surface: Coastal wardens routinely spotted seabirds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernes, or erns, are sea eagles, large birds of the coast.

clue.text: Happy, perhaps, and content to read war fiction

indicators.note: content means what is contained, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: Someone happy and satisfied to read novels about war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' looks like a mood, and 'content' backs that up; Happy is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, an example of the type.

clue.text: Raver, rattling on outside, went on too long

indicators.note: outside means the word on wraps round the shaken letters
rattling shakes the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A partygoer rambling on outside stayed too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling on' reads as chattering, but 'rattling' shuffles the partygoer and 'outside' wraps the little word round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go past the allotted time; overran is its past tense.

clue.text: Never to be forgotten with the passing of time? Wrong

indicators.note: passing means going away, so the time letter departs

parts.note: immortal means remembered for ever

explanation.surface: A musing on whether fame fades over time, then a verdict of 'wrong'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The passing of time' reads as years going by; here T passes out of IMMORTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means morally wrong, against accepted standards of conduct.

clue.text: Boss has mate round

indicators.note: round signals that the mating word is turned around

parts.note: to mate is, in slang, to bonk

explanation.surface: The manager has a friend over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager and 'mate' a friend; a boss is a raised stud, and mate is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round knob or stud projecting from a surface, such as a shield.

clue.text: Left home to visit relative

indicators.note: to visit is to go into, so the home word enters the relative

parts.note: a sister is a relative
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone left the house to call on a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is the heraldic and Latin sense, on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister comes from the Latin for left and means the left-hand side in heraldry.
